title: Second-order geometry of optimal transport: cost identifiability and stability
summary: We study the optimal transport value as a functional of the ground cost. Although this functional is an infimum of linear functionals and is therefore polyhedral for finitely supported marginals, it develops genuine second-order geometry in the smooth continuous setting. Under twist, nondegeneracy, and regularity assumptions, we prove twice differentiability with respect to the cost in Hölder spaces, derive a variational formula for the Hessian, and characterize its null space. The resulting curvature is strict transverse to the cost perturbations that preserve the observed optimal plan.…
